doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Joining the Messengers and moving to New York
title: Playing behind Monk, Griffin and Art Farmer at the Beehive
summary: As house rhythm section Ware backs Thelonious Monk, whom he meets for the first time, then Art Farmer, before missing gigs because of drugs.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: The next group to come in -- well, it wasn't a group so what Sol was doing, we were working the off nights, the trio -- rhythm section; piano, bass and drum, and here comes Themonius.
That following Wednesday, that following week. And Sol said, "Well, you know, you're the house rhythm section" -- so that meant we had to play behind Thelonious.
So, Jody was off, so they all said, "Well, who are we gonna get?" So Wilbur Wilt said, "Well, let's get Griffin." And I said, "Good idea!" the following week So I remember Griff came in ...

Quartet. And that was my introduction to Thelonious, and with five of us Wilbur and I why, we'd hang out all during the week. And he said, "How come I never saw you when I came to Chicago?" Well, what could I tell him? This is Thelonious, the first time I ever meet the guy, and I'm standing in awe of this giant. But he was a beautiful person, you know? And I remember that well, because at the end of the week, he received a telegram from his wife saying his mother died, and wanted him to come home right away.

He says, "Well, "I left New York when mama was alive and I don't want to go back and see her in the casket and all that ..." because Sol had asked him to stay over an extra 2 nights to work with us, which he did. And the following week, here come -- we played behind Art Farmer -- Jody, and we hired little John Jenkins on alto, you know, and that went on - and anyway, I fooled around, and I didn't show up -- Drugs had something to do with that.
